help.title: How to use this page
help.intro: Run a Python snippet against your data and see whatever it print()s — quick stats, grouping, exports, anything pandas can do.
help.step1: Pick the data — Grid data uses every row currently in the Query tab's table (query result or uploaded file); Snapshot data runs against a stored snapshot instead.
help.step2: Write Python — your rows arrive in a variable named data (a list of dicts, one per row). pandas is pre-installed: import pandas as pd.
help.step3: Run script — the output panel shows what the script printed (errors included). Files the script saves land in your Downloads folder — see the Excel example.
help.step4: Reuse — Insert example loads ready-made snippets, Use template / View opens the shared template library, and Save + Custom keep your own scripts one click away.
help.tipTitle: Tip — let Copilot (or any AI) write the script for you
help.tipIntro: Ask an external LLM such as M365 Copilot Chat, and give it three things:
help.tipTask: the task you want done — e.g. “top 10 HOLD_CODEs by row count”,
help.tipContract: the contract — rows come in data (a list of dicts), pandas is available, results are shown via print(),
help.tipSample: a sample of your data — upload a sample file or copy a few rows from the grid and paste them in.
help.tipOutro: The prompt below already covers the contract — it also tells the AI to build an HTML report with Apache ECharts charts, save it to your Downloads folder, open it when done, and (when the task needs your input) show a native Windows dialog the same way this app does. Fill in the task plus the uploaded or pasted sample data:
help.copilotPrompt:
Write a Python 3 script for the ODBC Query App "Script" tab.

Context: this script will be executed automatically inside the app (not run by a human from a terminal) — there is no command line, no stdin, and no user typing input while it runs.

Contract:
- My query result is already loaded in a variable called data — a list of dicts, one dict per row, e.g. [{'LOT_ID': 'A123', 'QTY': 10}, ...].
- pandas is available (import pandas as pd). Built-ins like math/json are fine.
- Use plain Python/pandas only; do not install packages or touch the database.

Output requirements:
- Present the result as a single self-contained HTML report (inline the data and tables directly in the HTML; no other external files or network calls).
- Use Apache ECharts for any charts. The app bundles it — do `from app.resources.echarts import get_echarts_js` and inline the returned JS into the HTML; do NOT use a CDN. Render each chart in its own sized <div>.
- Save the HTML file into the user's Downloads folder, falling back to the OS temp folder if Downloads is not writable (probe writability first), using an absolute path with a timestamped filename like report_YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS.html.
- After writing the file, open it in the default browser with webbrowser.open(Path(path).as_uri()).
- Also print() a short confirmation (and any key findings) so the app's output panel shows what happened.

Interactive dialogs (only if the task needs to ask the user something):
- The script runs non-interactively (no stdin) and tkinter is NOT available, so do NOT use input(), tkinter or console prompts.
- Follow the app's practice: launch a native Windows dialog as a child process — write the choices to a JSON file in a temp dir, run a PowerShell + WinForms script via subprocess.run([powershell, "-NoProfile", "-STA", "-ExecutionPolicy", "Bypass", "-File", ps_path, in_path, out_path], creationflags=subprocess.CREATE_NO_WINDOW), then read the user's selection back from another JSON file.
- Guard it: skip the dialog when os.name != "nt" or PowerShell is missing, support an env-var skip, apply a timeout, and fall back to sensible defaults instead of failing.

Task: <describe what you want, e.g. "count rows per HOLD_CODE, sort by count, show the top 10">

My data (columns plus a few sample rows, copied from the grid):
<paste a handful of rows here>
